chunks: From him, from al-Sayyari, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said:

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man divorced his wife and called two Nasibiyyah (those who oppose the Ahl al-Bayt) as witnesses. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Every person who is born upon the natural disposition (fitrah) and is known to be righteous in himself, his testimony is valid.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: The natural disposition or innate state of creation
key_terms.نَاصِبِيَّيْنِ: Two individuals known for opposing the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: Are Nasibiyyah witnesses valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that the testimony of two 'Nasibiyyah' is valid in divorce proceedings provided they are recognized for personal righteousness and born upon the natural fitrah, demonstrating that specific theological opposition does not automatically invalidate legal credibility. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between doctrinal enmity (Nasb) and moral integrity (Adalah), prioritizing observable character over sectarian affiliation in judicial contexts. It underscores the flexibility of the 'Ahl al-Bayt' school in accepting diverse witnesses for civil matters while maintaining theological distinctiveness.
